name: Pfarrkirche St. Andreas
kurzbeschreibung: The late-Gothic Saint Andreas Parish Church in Kitzbühel showcases magnificent baroque altars, ceiling frescoes, and the adjoining historic Liebfrauen Bell Tower.
preis: Free admission (donations toward the conservation of historical sacred art appreciated)
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round daily from approx. 08:00 to 18:00 for visits and prayer
beschreibung:
Overview

The Roman Catholic Saint Andreas Parish Church (Stadtpfarrkirche Sankt Andreas) crowns a gentle elevation on the northern perimeter of Kitzbühel's historic old town, forming a prominent sacred architectural ensemble alongside the neighboring Liebfrauen Church. Erected between 1435 and 1506 upon the foundations of earlier Romanesque structures, the church exemplifies late-Gothic Tyrolean ecclesiastical architecture in its purest form. During the 17th and 18th centuries, the interior received an opulent Baroque transformation, endowing the three-aisled hall church with remarkable solemn dignity, masterly wood carving, and enduring spiritual allure.

Route & Requirements

From Kitzbühel's town centre, a short incline leads via Kirchgasse and through the atmospheric walled town cemetery directly to the main church portals. Inside, the monumental high baroque altar from the late 17th century commands immediate attention. Outstanding features include the ceiling frescoes and finely carved wooden statues created by masters of the renowned Kitzbühel sculptural school, such as Benedikt Faistenberger. A quiet walk through the meticulously kept cemetery passes ornate wrought-iron grave crosses of historic local families and ski pioneers to reach the two-storey Liebfrauen Church with its ringing bells. Access is straightforward with only a few stone steps; ordinary walking shoes are suitable.

Visit & Arrival

The parish church is open to visitors daily year-round from around 08:00 to 18:00, outside of scheduled religious services, weddings, or funerals. Admission is completely free, though donations for heritage preservation are warmly appreciated. Arrival by public transit: Kitzbühel main railway station and Kitzbühel Hahnenkammbahn stop are served frequently by ÖBB regional and express trains; from there it is a pleasant ten-minute walk through town. By car, follow the Pass-Thurn-Straße B161 into town; paid parking is available at the nearby Pfarrau car park or Zentrum parking garage.

Tips

Be sure to visit the Gothic Liebfrauen Church right beside the parish church; its mighty tower houses the celebrated „Kitzbüheler Glocke“, praised as one of the most melodious historical bronze church bells in all of Austria. A stroll through the heritage cemetery also rewards visitors with sublime panoramic vistas of the Kitzbüheler Horn and the world-famous Hahnenkamm slope. The sacred complex is beautifully lit after dusk.
